_comment: Bounds known from the literature but NOT verified in this repo. Each entry is a task waiting to happen: replace it with a Lean proof or a certificate. Sources marked 'read' were checked against the paper text by an audit agent on 2026-11-20, not by a human. The scoreboard's literature column assumes a field of characteristic 0; see 'hypotheses'.
hypotheses: In characteristic 2 the permanent equals the determinant, so dc(perm_n) = n and none of the lower bounds below apply. The Lean library works over an arbitrary commutative ring; any Lean statement of these bounds must add the field and characteristic hypothesis.

lower.source: Alper, Bogart, Velasco, A lower bound for the determinantal complexity of a hypersurface, arXiv:1505.02205, Corollary 1.4 (read)
Mignon, Ressayre, A quadratic bound for the determinant and permanent problem, 2004 (statement confirmed only as quoted in later papers; task T-008)

upper.field: any commutative ring (the paper states characteristic != 2; the construction is characteristic-free)
upper.source: Grenet, An upper bound for the permanent versus determinant problem, manuscript 2011 (read; task T-007; certificates here for n <= 4)

not_on_the_board_yet.claim: dc(perm_n) >= (n-1)^2 + 1 over the real numbers, which would give 10 for n = 4 and 17 for n = 5
not_on_the_board_yet.source: Yabe, Bi-polynomial rank and determinantal complexity, arXiv:1504.00151 (abstract only; refereed status not checked)

not_on_the_board_yet.claim: dc(perm_n) >= (n-2)(n-3)/2 over any field of characteristic != 2
not_on_the_board_yet.source: Cai, Chen, Li, Quadratic lower bound for permanent vs. determinant in any characteristic, computational complexity 19 (2010) (abstract and introduction read; the explicit bound only as quoted elsewhere)

not_on_the_board_yet.claim: dc(perm_n) >= n + 1 for n >= 3 in characteristic 0
not_on_the_board_yet.source: Marcus, Minc 1961 (only as quoted in Cai, Chen, Li)

not_on_the_board_yet.claim: with entries restricted to 0, 1 and variables, perm_3 needs size 7
not_on_the_board_yet.source: Hüttenhain, Ikenmeyer, Binary determinantal complexity, arXiv:1410.8202 (abstract read)
